problem: Existing VLN-CE methods (CWP-RecBERT, GridMM, ETPNav) port discrete VLN pipelines to continuous environments and ignore collisions: predicted waypoints can lie inside obstacles and the agent gets stuck en route, deviating from the plan or failing. ETPNav's 'Tryout' heuristic only tweaks low-level control and still leaves the agent trapped.
motivation: Collisions are frequent in VLN-CE and hurt success. Robust collision handling is needed before VLN can be deployed on real robots. The paper observes that collisions arise from distinct causes (bad waypoints, obstacles on the path, dynamic changes), each needing a different fix.
key_idea: Classify VLN-CE collisions into waypoint, navigation and dynamic types, then mask the waypoint heatmap with a simulated 2D LiDAR occupancy mask and train a navigator to re-select a sub-optimal waypoint after a collision.
insight: The re-selection navigator drives most of the collision reduction: N-C on ETPNav falls from 14.0 to 4.3 when Safe-VLN is added, whereas the occupancy mask alone changes N-C and W-C only slightly (ablation Table 3). Gains are mostly in SR and collision rates, while SPL often drops (ETPNav 49.0 to 47.8) because detours lengthen paths. Richer sensing does not always help: 3D LiDAR at 1.0m and 2D+3D fusion were worse than 2D, likely due to reconstruction errors in the simulated scans. The mask weight δ must stay small (≤1e-4), because larger values wrongly mask free space.
method: Collision taxonomy: three types. Waypoint collision means the predicted waypoint is inside an obstacle. Navigation collision means the agent hits obstacles while moving to the next waypoint. Dynamic collision means a chosen waypoint becomes non-navigable, simulated by making the selected waypoint non-navigable with 10% probability.

Occupancy mask: a simulated 360° 2D LiDAR built from depth (3m range, 12 range bins of 0.25m, 120 heading bins of 3°) gives a mask M_t (-1 for occupied, 0 otherwise). The heatmap is updated as H*_t = norm(H_t + δ·M_t), with δ=1e-4, before NMS sampling of the K waypoints from ETPNav's waypoint predictor.

Re-selection navigator: ETPNav-style topological graph planner with a cross-modal transformer scoring nodes, including ghost nodes. After a collision or non-navigable waypoint, the agent re-selects the next-best waypoint instead of getting stuck. It combines with the 'Tryout' mechanism, and re-selection is used if Tryout fails.
Sub-optimal supervision: the loss adds a term for the second-shortest-path action, L_p = Σ[λ1 log p(a1)+λ2 log p(a2)], with λ1=0.8 and λ2=0.2.
Plug-in usage: Safe-VLN can be added at validation without retraining to CWP-RecBERT, GridMM and ETPNav, or ETPNav can be fine-tuned with it (20k iterations, 2×3090Ti, ~50h). Cycle time is ~0.4s.
New metrics: N-C (navigation collision step ratio), W-C (ratio of candidate waypoints in collision areas) and D-C SR (SR under dynamic collisions).

setting.backbone: ETPNav (waypoint predictor + topological cross-modal transformer planner; CLIP ViT RGB encoder, ResNet depth encoder), fine-tuned with Safe-VLN
setting.training_data: R2R-CE training split; ETPNav fine-tuned for 20,000 iterations with the sub-optimal action loss and occupancy mask; no extra data
setting.observation: 12-view panoramic RGB-D (30° spacing), agent position, simulated 2D LiDAR occupancy from depth
setting.action_space: Low-level FORWARD 0.25m / TURN-LEFT 15° / TURN-RIGHT 15° / STOP, with high-level waypoint selection on a topological graph
setting.privileged: Agent position available; simulated LiDAR derived from simulator depth; no GT map

results: Fine-tuned Safe-VLN reaches R2R-CE val-unseen SR 60 / SPL 47 and test-unseen SR 56 / SPL 45. This gives higher SR than ETPNav (57 / 55) but lower SPL (49 / 48). As an inference-only plug-in it raises SR for CWP-RecBERT (44.0 to 44.9), GridMM (48.5 to 49.4) and ETPNav (57.1 to 57.9), and cuts N-C sharply (ETPNav 14.0 to 4.3). It also beats a JPS grid-map navigator (SR 44.8, SPL 26.4) and is about 8x faster.
limitations: Only evaluated in simulation; sim-to-real transfer and real LiDAR are future work
SPL usually drops (ETPNav 49.0 to 47.8; 49 to 47 val-unseen) and SR gains are small (~1 point), while the simulated LiDAR is noisy from mesh reconstruction errors
Dynamic collisions are synthetic (10% random non-navigable waypoint), not from a real dynamic-obstacle dataset
